facts.statement: Tethyshadros lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Campanian age.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous (Campanian)

facts.statement: This dinosaur is found in the Lipica Formation near Trieste, Italy, and was previously thought to belong to the Liburnia Formation.
facts.quote: Tethyshadros ("Tethyan hadrosauroid") is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) Lipica Formation (previously thought to come from the younger informal "Liburnia Formation") of Trieste, Italy.

facts.statement: The main skeleton of Tethyshadros was not fully extracted from the quarry until 1999.
facts.quote: The main skeleton was not extracted until 1999.

facts.statement: The genus Tethyshadros was named and described by Dalla Vecchia in 2009.
facts.quote: The genus was named and described by Dalla Vecchia in 2009.

facts.statement: The genus name combines a reference to the Tethys Ocean and the group Hadrosauroidea.
facts.quote: The genus name refers to the Tethys Ocean and the Hadrosauroidea.

facts.statement: The species name means "insular" or "of the island," referring to the animal's habitat on islands in the European Archipelago.
facts.quote: The specific name means "insular" or "of the island" in Latin, a reference to the fact that species would have lived on one of the larger islands of the European Archipelago.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, nicknamed "Antonio," is a mostly complete but crushed skeleton cataloged as SC 57021.
facts.quote: The holotype of the genus is SC 57021 (Antonio), a mostly complete but crushed skeleton.

facts.statement: An additional extensive skeleton nicknamed "Bruno" (SC 57247) was found at the same site.
facts.quote: An additional extensive skeleton of Tethyshadros was found at this site, SC 57247, nicknamed "Bruno".

facts.statement: Multiple specimens lived at different times, with individuals separated by a maximum of a few thousand years within a geologic lens deposited over less than 10,000 years.
facts.quote: Each specimen was deposited in a different level of the geologic lens, so they each lived at different times; the lens is thought to have been deposited over less than 10,000 years, meaning the individuals lived a maximum of a few thousand years apart from each other.

facts.statement: Preparing the fossil specimen required 2,800 hours of work to remove it from the rock matrix.
facts.quote: The specimen underwent 2800 hours of preparation (the process of removing the fossil from the rock matrix).

facts.statement: The total estimated body length is 4.5 meters, though some argue this figure is an overestimate.
facts.quote: The length of the tail including the unpreserved portion was later estimated to be 2.5 m, resulting in a total estimated body length of 4.5 m for the animal, though it's been argued this is an overestimate.

facts.statement: The subadult holotype "Antonio" weighed approximately 338 kg, while the adult "Bruno" weighed between 514 and 584 kg.
facts.quote: Antonio has been estimated at 338 kg in weight, while Bruno has been estimated at 514 - 584 kg.

facts.statement: This dinosaur had a beak, hands formed into fleshy pads, and three-toed feet.
facts.quote: Tethyshadros was a beaked animal with a hand formed into a fleshy pad and three-toed feet.

facts.statement: Tethyshadros possesses a large number of autapomorphies, which are anatomical features unique to this species.
facts.quote: It possesses a large number of autapomorphies, or anatomical features entirely unique to this species.

facts.statement: Originally, the skull had seven unique traits, the vertebral column had seven, and the limbs had six unique traits.
facts.quote: Specifically, it was originally described with the skull possessing seven such traits, the vertebral column seven, and the limbs six.

facts.statement: Its anatomy shows an intermediary nature, mixing primitive and derived features.
facts.quote: Another prominent aspect of Tethyshadros anatomy is its intermediary nature – it possesses a mixture of primitive features and derived features.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the holotype represented an adult or a subadult, with later assessments based on bone histology suggesting it was a subadult.
facts.quote: Although the holotype Antonio was initially thought to represent an adult, it was later assessed to be a subadult individual based on the histology of its bones.

facts.statement: In 2021, researchers placed Tethyshadros as the sister taxon to Fylax within the Hadrosauromorpha clade.
facts.quote: In 2021, Prieto-Márquez and Carrera Farias recovered Tethyshadros as the sister taxon to Fylax, in a derived position in the Hadrosauromorpha

facts.statement: In 2026, Magyar and colleagues recovered Tethyshadros as the sister taxon to Kryptohadros using updated phylogenetic matrices.
facts.quote: In their 2026 description of the Transylvanian Kryptohadros from the Hațeg Basin, Magyar and colleagues included it in an updated version of the phylogenetic matrix of Longrich et al. (2024) and the similar but less extensive matrix of Dai et al. (2025). Both datasets consistently recovered Tethyshadros as the sister taxon to Kryptohadros.

facts.statement: Magyar et al. named the clade containing Tethyshadros, Kryptohadros, and Telmatosaurus as Telmatosauridae.
facts.quote: Telmatosaurus, another Hațeg genus coeval with Kryptohadros, was recovered as the sister to these two taxa using both datasets. Magyar et al. named the group containing these three genera as the new clade Telmatosauridae.

facts.statement: The genus Tethyshadros was named by Dalla Vecchia in 2009.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Dalla Vecchia, 2009

facts.statement: Tethyshadros lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: The preserved part of the holotype specimen of Tethyshadros measures 3.6 meters in length.
facts.quote: Originalmente se pensó que Tethyshadros era un hadrosauroide enano. La parte conservada del holotipo mide 3,6 m y solo falta el extremo de la cola.

facts.statement: The total estimated body length of Tethyshadros is 4.5 meters, though some argue this is an overestimation.
facts.quote: Posteriormente, se estimó que la longitud de la cola, incluida la parte no preservada, era de 2,5 m, lo que resultó en una longitud corporal total estimada de 4,5 m para el animal, aunque se ha argumentado que esto es una sobreestimación.

facts.statement: The specimen "Bruno" is between 15% and 20% larger than "Antonio" and displays adult characteristics such as a more robust skull.
facts.quote: Se descubrió que "Bruno", que es entre un 15% y un 20% más grande que "Antonio", es un adulto y muestra características relacionadas con la madurez, como un cráneo más robusto y proporciones más robustas.

facts.statement: The estimated weight of the holotype "Antonio" is 338 kg, while "Bruno" is estimated at 514 to 584 kg.
facts.quote: "Antonio" se ha estimado en 338 kg de peso, mientras que Bruno se ha estimado en 514 a 584 kg.

facts.statement: Tethyshadros had a beak, a hand formed into a fleshy pad, and three-toed feet.
facts.quote: Siendo un hadrosauroideo, Tethyshadros era un animal con pico, con una mano formada en una almohadilla carnosa y pies de tres dedos.

facts.statement: Tethyshadros was originally described as having seven unique cranial traits, seven unique vertebral traits, and six unique limb traits.
facts.quote: Específicamente, se describió originalmente con el cráneo que poseía siete de esos rasgos, la columna vertebral siete y las extremidades seis.

facts.statement: Tethyshadros resembles earlier relatives like Iguanodon in skull shape, possession of a supraorbital bone, and a comparatively short neck.
facts.quote: De alguna manera, la especie se parece más a parientes anteriores como Iguanodon, como en la forma general del cráneo, la posesión de un hueso supraorbitario y el cuello comparativamente corto.

facts.statement: Tethyshadros is comparable to true hadrosaurids in hand morphology, lack of an anteorbital fenestra, and teeth arranged in batteries.
facts.quote: En otros, es más comparable a la condición que se observa en los verdaderos hadrosáuridos, tal como se aprecia con su morfología de mano, falta de fenestra anteorbitaria y dientes dispuestos en baterías.

facts.statement: A nearly complete skeleton of a hadrosauroid was discovered in 1994 at an abandoned quarry in Villaggio del Pescatore, Italy.
facts.quote: Fue en esta cantera donde se descubrió un esqueleto de hadrosauroide casi completo en 1994.

facts.statement: The main skeleton was not fully excavated until 1999.
facts.quote: El esqueleto principal no se extrajo hasta 1999.

facts.statement: The discovery was immediately recognized as the oldest known hadrosauroid in Europe and the most complete large dinosaur skeleton found on the continent since the Iguanodon remains in Belgium.
facts.quote: La importancia del hallazgo se reconoció de inmediato, siendo el hadrosauroide más antiguo conocido en Europa y el esqueleto de dinosaurio grande más completo encontrado en el continente desde el descubrimiento del de los restos de Iguanodon en Bernissart, Bélgica.

facts.statement: Based on associated fossils and geological data, the hadrosauroid dates to the Campanian stage at the boundary with the Maastrichtian, approximately 70 million years ago, though recent studies revise this age to 81.5–80.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Basado en la presencia de foraminíferos Murciella cuvillieri y el aligatoroideo Acynodon, además de datos geológicos, el fósil de hadrosáurido data del Campaniense en el límite con el Maastrichtiense, hace unos 70 millones de años, una edad recientemente revaluada por estudios más recientes hasta hace 81,5-80,5 millones de años.

facts.statement: The excavation block containing the specimen weighed five tons and was too large to transport as a single unit.
facts.quote: Una vez finalizada la excavación, el bloque de cinco toneladas que contenía el espécimen resultó demasiado grande para el transporte.

facts.statement: The main specimen was given the nickname "Antonio" in press reports after its public presentation.
facts.quote: Fue en este punto que el ejemplar ganó el apodo de "Antonio", que se le da en los informes de prensa.

facts.statement: The genus was named and described by Dalla Vecchia in 2009.
facts.quote: El género fue nombrado y descrito por Dalla Vecchia en 2009.

facts.statement: Growth lines in the bones indicate that the holotype specimen was between 5 and 6 years old when it died.
facts.quote: Las líneas de crecimiento en los huesos indican que el ejemplar habría tenido entre 5 a 6 años a la hora de su muerte.

facts.statement: An additional extensive skeleton of Tethyshadros, nicknamed "Bruno," was found at the site with catalog number SC 57247.
facts.quote: En este sitio, SC 57247, se encontró un esqueleto extenso adicional de Tethyshadros, apodado "Bruno".

facts.statement: "Bruno" along with five other specimens was formally described in 2021 by Alfio Alessandro Chiarenza and colleagues.
facts.quote: "Bruno", junto con otros cinco especímenes, fue descrito formalmente en 2021 por Alfio Alessandro Chiarenza y sus colegas.

facts.statement: Each specimen was deposited in a different level of the geological lens, meaning they lived in different time periods.
facts.quote: Cada espécimen fue depositado en un nivel diferente de la lente geológica, por lo que cada uno vivió en diferentes épocas.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis indicated that Tethyshadros was closely related to Hadrosauridae sensu Sereno and Telmatosaurus.
facts.quote: El análisis cladistico indicó que estaba estrechamente vinculado a Hadrosauridae sensu Sereno y a Telmatosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2021, Prieto-Márquez and Carrera Farias recovered Tethyshadros as the sister taxon of Fylax in a derived position within Hadrosauromorpha, making it one of the last surviving non-hadrosaurid hadrosauromorphs.
facts.quote: En 2021, Prieto-Márquez y Carrera Farias recuperaron a Tethyshadros como el taxón hermano de Fylax, en una posición derivada en Hadrosauromorpha, convirtiéndolo en uno de los últimos hadrosauromorfos no hadrosáuridos supervivientes.

facts.statement: A 2021 phylogenetic analysis of "Bruno" by Chiarenza et al. found Tethyshadros in a similar position, except that Telmatosaurus appeared as its closest relative.
facts.quote: Chiarenza et al 2021 realizaron un análisis filogenético de Bruno. Este análisis encontró a Tethyshadros en una posición similar, excepto que Telmatosaurus aparece como su pariente más cercano.

facts.statement: Other close relatives were generally Asian or North American species.
facts.quote: Otros parientes cercanos eran generalmente especies asiáticas o norteamericanas.

facts.statement: Body size evolution modeling suggested that Tethyshadros was not significantly different in size from its closest relatives.
facts.quote: El modelado de la evolución del tamaño del cuerpo sugirió que Tethyshadros no era significativamente diferente en tamaño de sus parientes más cercanos.

facts.statement: The parent group of Tethyshadros is Telmatosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Telmatosauridae

facts.statement: Tethyshadros belongs to the family Telmatosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Telmatosauridae

facts.statement: Tethyshadros is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The time range for Tethyshadros is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Dalla Vecchia rejected the possibility that the species was a remnant of isolated evolution of earlier European hadrosauroids or descended from American hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: De esta manera rechaza la posibilidad de que la especie sea un residuo de la evolución aislada de hadrosauroides europeos anteriores o que descienda de hadrosáuridos americanos.

facts.statement: A 2020 description by Della Vacchia focusing on the tail anatomy was mostly refuted in subsequent studies.
facts.quote: Della Vacchia publicó una descripción adicional de la especie, centrándose específicamente en la anatomía de su cola, en 2020, que fue refutada en su mayoría en los siguientes estudios.
